label: help
text:
Usage: reaktor [<options>]

  Reaktor workspace operations, generated from the graph-owned catalog. Browse:
  build list; build tree; build explain NODE. Verify: build plan NODE; build
  run NODE. Inspect: run list; run show RUN; run logs RUN. Discover: operation
  catalog; operation describe OPERATION. Phones: connect ios; connect android.
  Independent physical-device trust, unlock and automation checks. Common
  options before or after commands: --dir DIRECTORY (--workspace during
  migration), --args JSON or -, --json, --detach, --request-id ID, --seat
  HARNESS. No validated catalog cached here. Run reaktor --dir WORKSPACE
  operation catalog explicitly to refresh it. Completion: completion
  bash|zsh|fish. MCP: mcp install; mcp --stdio --seat HARNESS. Help, version
  and static completion never start an owner.

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit

label: agent-help
text:
reaktor-agent - workspace lifecycle, Atlas and standalone agent protocols.
Use reaktor for build, check, deploy, runs and other workspace operations.

  workspace           workspace owner, MCP, browser pairing and agent lifecycle
  atlas               code queries, source reads, change plans and checks
  usage [--since <ISO-date>] [--until <ISO-date>] [--dir <cwd-root>] [--requests <new.jsonl>]
                      read local Codex/Claude request usage; defaults to the last seven days

  --prompt <text>      the task (required)
  --dir <path>         working directory the agents read (default: current directory)
  --protocol <name>    ask | all | council | pipeline | planned   (default: ask)
  --plan <file>        a Protocol as JSON: your own topology, used instead of --protocol
  --agents <a,b,c>     agent ids to involve (default: every participant)
  --roster <file>      JSON array of AgentSpec: your own agents (default: a small sample roster)
  --thread <file>      read and write the canonical thread here
  --context <file>     scoped ContextPacket JSON (e.g. Manna context_for_task result data)
  --dry                use the offline Echo runtime; spawns nothing
  --isolate-config     run harnesses without your own config (reproducible; ignores your setup)
  --quiet              do not stream agent output

The built-in roster and pipeline are samples. Real use is --roster with your own agents and
--plan with your own topology, or --protocol planned to let an agent design both.

Examples:
  --protocol council --prompt "Should reaktor-db own sync, or should reaktor-service?"
  --roster team.json --plan review.json --prompt "Harden the notification path"
  --protocol planned --agents architect --prompt "Port the FFI wire to credit backpressure"
  --protocol ask --agents skeptic --prompt "What breaks in this design?"
